result:
Only Solution 3 survives a parity check on $\nu$, and its value of 3 matches my partial recollection of the literature, so I choose it. I did not derive the value independently.

**Parity check.** The Crowley–Nordström invariant satisfies $\nu \equiv \chi(W) - 3\sigma(W) \equiv \chi(W) + \sigma(W) \pmod 2$ for a Spin(7) coboundary $W$. This parity equals the real semi-characteristic of the boundary, $b_0+b_1+b_2+b_3$.

For $N_{k,l}$, $H^2$ is finite, namely $\mathbb{Z}/(k^2+kl+l^2)$. So $b_2 = 0$, and also $b_1 = b_3 = 0$. The semi-characteristic is therefore $1$, which is odd. Hence $\nu$, and so $\bar\nu$, must be odd.

**Solution 1** gives $0$, which is even, so it is wrong. Its argument also fails because the Killing-spinor correction term does not vanish. The complex-conjugation symmetry does not make the full invariant zero.

**Solution 2** gives $6$, which is even, so it is wrong. It uses $b_2 = 1$, but $N_{k,l}$ has $b_2 = 0$. Its disc-bundle computation also treats $N_{k,l}$ as bounding a disc bundle over the flag manifold, which does not give a valid Spin(7) coboundary here.

**Solution 3** gives $3$, which is odd and so passes the parity check. It also matches my recollection of the Crowley–Goette–Nordström result, which is independent of $(k,l)$.

CHOICE: 3
